world.title: Costa Rica bars U.N. rapporteur Albanese; court blocks removal
world.summary: Costa Rica refused entry to Francesca Albanese, the United Nations’ special rapporteur on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories, at San José’s airport on Thursday, Nov. 26, citing an “international alert” over alleged links to terrorist acts. Immigration chief Omer Badilla did not say who issued the aler
world.content: Costa Rica refused entry to Francesca Albanese, the United Nations’ special rapporteur on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories, at San José’s airport on Thursday, Nov. 26, citing an “international alert” over alleged links to terrorist acts. Immigration chief Omer Badilla did not say who issued the alert or provide evidence for the allegation. Albanese had traveled to receive an honorary doctorate from the University of Costa Rica, whose leaders demanded a public explanation and guarantees of due process. Albanese rejected the accusation and called on the government to substantiate it or apologize. Costa Rica’s Constitutional Court issued an interim order barring authorities from forcibly removing her while it considers a habeas corpus petition. It also ordered immigration officials to submit a sworn account within 24 hours.
world.image_alt: Costa Rica bars U.N. rapporteur Albanese; court blocks removal

world.title: Batumi football match halted after clashes over Palestinian flag
world.summary: A Europa League match between Turkish club Beşiktaş and Israel’s Hapoel Beer-Sheva was halted for about 30 minutes in Batumi, Georgia, on Thursday after Turkish supporters clashed with Georgian police. The disturbance began in the 25th or 26th minute. Play resumed, and Beşiktaş won 2-1. The fixture had been moved from
world.content: A Europa League match between Turkish club Beşiktaş and Israel’s Hapoel Beer-Sheva was halted for about 30 minutes in Batumi, Georgia, on Thursday after Turkish supporters clashed with Georgian police. The disturbance began in the 25th or 26th minute. Play resumed, and Beşiktaş won 2-1. The fixture had been moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities said security concerns made it unsafe to host the match there. Beşiktaş said police used disproportionate force against its fans and lodged a complaint with UEFA, European football’s governing body. Georgia’s Interior Ministry disputed the club’s account, saying clashes began before Palestinian flags and banners appeared and that supporters threw seats at officers. Turkey’s foreign minister spoke with his Georgian counterpart after the clashes. UEFA said it would assess the events on Friday, November 27.
world.image_alt: Batumi football match halted after clashes over Palestinian flag

world.title: Eisenkot secures left-wing coalition deal but still lacks majority
world.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the centrist Yashar party leader tasked with forming Israel’s next government, reached a coalition agreement on Nov. 26 with the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, in his bid to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Democrats say they will receive four ministerial portfolios: publ
world.content: Gadi Eisenkot, the centrist Yashar party leader tasked with forming Israel’s next government, reached a coalition agreement on Nov. 26 with the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, in his bid to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Democrats say they will receive four ministerial portfolios: public security, labour, communications, and culture and sport. The culture and sport ministry would include a new directorate for democracy. The agreement follows a deal with Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Israel Beiteinu party, but the three parties together hold only 36 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett’s Beyachad party holds 12 seats and is part of the wider opposition bloc, but has not signed a formal coalition agreement with Yashar. Eisenkot’s camp remains divided over whether to rely on Arab-majority parties, negotiate with ultra-Orthodox parties or pursue a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud. Eisenkot has until Dec. 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension from President Isaac Herzog.
world.image_alt: Eisenkot secures left-wing coalition deal but still lacks majority

world.title: Guinea-Bissau junta delays presidential and parliamentary elections until 2028
world.summary: Guinea-Bissau’s military government has postponed presidential and parliamentary elections until Nov. 26, 2028, extending its promised one-year transition to civilian rule by about two years. Transitional President Gen. Horta N’Tam set the date in a Nov. 26 decree on the anniversary of the 2025 coup. The elections had
world.content: Guinea-Bissau’s military government has postponed presidential and parliamentary elections until Nov. 26, 2028, extending its promised one-year transition to civilian rule by about two years. Transitional President Gen. Horta N’Tam set the date in a Nov. 26 decree on the anniversary of the 2025 coup. The elections had been scheduled for Dec. 6, 2026. The junta said technical, material and financial preparations were inadequate to ensure a credible vote. The army seized power three days after the November 2025 general election, before officials announced the results. Incumbent President Umaro Sissoco Embaló and opposition candidate Fernando Dias both claimed victory. In August 2026, voters approved a military-organized constitutional referendum that strengthened presidential powers and reduced the size of parliament; the opposition had called for a boycott. N’Tam said the transition required more time and resources for electoral reforms, including a nationwide voter census and new constituency boundaries. The junta also says it needs to hold the country’s first municipal elections in 2027. The regional bloc ECOWAS has urged a short, structured and transparent return to civilian rule.
world.image_alt: Guinea-Bissau junta delays presidential and parliamentary elections until 2028

world.title: UK net migration falls to lowest level since 1997 outside pandemic
world.summary: Britain’s net long-term migration fell to 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, the lowest level since 1997 outside the pandemic, the Office for National Statistics said. The figure was down 62% from 204,000 a year earlier and 92% from the peak of 944,000 in the year ending March 2023. An estimated 738,000 people moved
world.content: Britain’s net long-term migration fell to 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, the lowest level since 1997 outside the pandemic, the Office for National Statistics said. The figure was down 62% from 204,000 a year earlier and 92% from the peak of 944,000 in the year ending March 2023. An estimated 738,000 people moved to the UK and 661,000 left. The decline largely reflects fewer arrivals from outside the European Union for work, study and asylum, following tighter visa rules introduced by Conservative governments and retained or expanded by Labour. Immigration fell 17% over the year, while emigration remained high. Analysts say those leaving include non-citizens who arrived during an earlier period of unusually high migration. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood credited Labour’s restrictions, while the Conservatives said measures introduced under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak drove much of the fall. Researchers cautioned that the unusually high level of emigration may not last and that fewer skilled-worker migrants could carry costs for the economy and public finances.
world.image_alt: UK net migration falls to lowest level since 1997 outside pandemic

world.title: French actor Gérard Depardieu ordered to face trial over 2018 rape allegation
world.summary: A Paris appeals court ruled on Nov. 26 that French actor Gérard Depardieu must stand trial for allegedly raping and sexually assaulting actress Charlotte Arnould at his Paris home on Aug. 7, 2018. It dismissed allegations concerning a second incident six days later. Depardieu, 77, denies the allegations and says the en
world.content: A Paris appeals court ruled on Nov. 26 that French actor Gérard Depardieu must stand trial for allegedly raping and sexually assaulting actress Charlotte Arnould at his Paris home on Aug. 7, 2018. It dismissed allegations concerning a second incident six days later. Depardieu, 77, denies the allegations and says the encounter was consensual. The ruling upheld part of an investigating judge’s 2025 order. On Nov. 16, Depardieu withdrew his appeal against a separate 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set. He accepted an 18-month suspended sentence and issued a public apology in that case. Depardieu’s lawyer David-Olivier Kaminski said the defense disputes the ruling and is considering an appeal to France’s Court of Cassation. The court has not announced a trial date. If convicted in the Arnould case, Depardieu could face up to 20 years in prison.
world.image_alt: French actor Gérard Depardieu ordered to face trial over 2018 rape allegation

world.title: Spanish banker Pablo Hernández de Cos chosen as next ECB president
world.summary: Eurozone leaders on Nov. 26 backed former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank (ECB), ending a contest with former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot. De Cos is due to take office on Feb. 7, 2027, when Lagarde leaves nine months before her
world.content: Eurozone leaders on Nov. 26 backed former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank (ECB), ending a contest with former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot. De Cos is due to take office on Feb. 7, 2027, when Lagarde leaves nine months before her term ends. Eurozone inflation stood at 4% in October, twice the ECB’s 2% target, with rising energy prices during the Iran war putting pressure on borrowing costs. Policymakers are widely expected to raise rates at their Dec. 17 meeting. France’s debt and budget disputes have also heightened concern that bond-market stress could spread across the currency bloc. The leadership agreement also names France’s Laurence Boone to oversee market operations and German economist Markus Brunnermeier as chief economist. EU leaders are expected to formally approve the appointments at their December summit, following consultations with the European Parliament and the ECB’s Governing Council. De Cos is scheduled to chair his first policy meeting on March 18.
world.image_alt: Spanish banker Pablo Hernández de Cos chosen as next ECB president

world.title: Spain votes Sunday with far-right Vox poised for national government role
world.summary: Spain votes on Nov. 29 in a snap parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s eight years in office and give far-right Vox its first role in a national government since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship ended in 1975. Pre-election polls put the conservative People’s Party (PP) near 31%, the Social
world.content: Spain votes on Nov. 29 in a snap parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s eight years in office and give far-right Vox its first role in a national government since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship ended in 1975. Pre-election polls put the conservative People’s Party (PP) near 31%, the Socialists (PSOE) around 29% to 30% and Vox at roughly 17% to 18%. The PP is expected to need Vox’s support to reach the 176 seats required for a majority in the 350-seat Congress. Sánchez called the early vote after parliament rejected housing measures on Oct. 2, amid anger over high rents and evictions. The campaign has also focused on corruption investigations involving people close to Sánchez, two fatal train crashes and migration, including the summer influx into the North African enclave of Ceuta. The PP and Vox have signaled changes to climate policy. Polling stations open at 9 a.m. local time and close at 8 p.m. If no bloc secures a majority, parties will have to negotiate support for a government.
world.image_alt: Spain votes Sunday with far-right Vox poised for national government role

business.title: Altria weighs cash bid for Imperial Brands as Japan Tobacco explores deal
business.summary: U.S. tobacco company Altria said on Nov. 26 it was considering an all-cash offer for British cigarette maker Imperial Brands and discussing a deal for part of the business with an unnamed third party. Japan Tobacco is also evaluating a possible acquisition, potentially with a partner and a division of Imperial’s assets
business.content: U.S. tobacco company Altria said on Nov. 26 it was considering an all-cash offer for British cigarette maker Imperial Brands and discussing a deal for part of the business with an unnamed third party. Japan Tobacco is also evaluating a possible acquisition, potentially with a partner and a division of Imperial’s assets. Imperial said it had received no approach from Altria or the unnamed third party but would consider any proposal. A transaction could return Altria to international cigarette sales, which it left after separating its overseas business two decades ago, and add established brands including Davidoff, Gauloises and Kool to a buyer’s portfolio. The companies are seeking growth as cigarette consumption declines and rivals Philip Morris International and British American Tobacco have moved further into newer nicotine products. Altria must make a firm offer or walk away by Dec. 24 under UK takeover rules.
business.image_alt: Altria weighs cash bid for Imperial Brands as Japan Tobacco explores deal

business.title: China pledges stronger stock-market support as shares rebound sharply
business.summary: China’s State Council on Friday pledged stronger support for the country’s stock market, directing state-backed investors to play a larger role in stabilizing shares and saying it would consider additional measures. The meeting, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, also called for more long-term investment in equities and enco
business.content: China’s State Council on Friday pledged stronger support for the country’s stock market, directing state-backed investors to play a larger role in stabilizing shares and saying it would consider additional measures. The meeting, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, also called for more long-term investment in equities and encouraged listed companies to increase dividends and share buybacks. The CSI 300 rose about 3.5% and the Shanghai Composite gained more than 3% after the announcement, which followed a slide that had taken major indexes to multi-month lows. The CSI 300 was still down 16% for 2026, with weak earnings and economic growth weighing on confidence. Officials gave no timetable for new support or details of its scale; separately, lower minimum margin requirements for leveraged stock purchases are due to take effect on Nov. 30.
business.image_alt: China pledges stronger stock-market support as shares rebound sharply

business.title: U.S. holiday retail sales forecast to top $1 trillion as shoppers cut back
business.summary: U.S. holiday retail sales are forecast to exceed $1 trillion this year, with the National Retail Federation projecting a 4.2% increase for November and December as Black Friday opens the peak shopping period. Inflation of 3.8% is expected to account for much of the increase, while 82% of consumers surveyed by the feder
business.content: U.S. holiday retail sales are forecast to exceed $1 trillion this year, with the National Retail Federation projecting a 4.2% increase for November and December as Black Friday opens the peak shopping period. Inflation of 3.8% is expected to account for much of the increase, while 82% of consumers surveyed by the federation said they were taking steps to control holiday costs, including buying less expensive gifts. Deloitte found that 87% of 1,200 consumers surveyed planned to shop during the five-day period ending on Cyber Monday, November 30, the highest share in a decade. UBS analysts said their holiday forecasts predated a stock-market correction and warned that falling asset values could curb affluent shoppers' spending. Retail consultant Ryan Orabone of Spaulding Ridge said pricing driven by artificial intelligence could push the deepest discounts closer to Christmas; the holiday shopping season runs through December 31.
business.image_alt: U.S. holiday retail sales forecast to top $1 trillion as shoppers cut back

business.title: Norse Atlantic suspends flights, warns of bankruptcy without urgent financing
business.summary: Norwegian low-cost long-haul carrier Norse Atlantic suspended all scheduled flights on Thursday, Nov. 26, and said its board intends to file for bankruptcy unless it urgently secures short-term financing. The airline is also discussing a possible takeover with investors but said it could not guarantee a viable solution
business.content: Norwegian low-cost long-haul carrier Norse Atlantic suspended all scheduled flights on Thursday, Nov. 26, and said its board intends to file for bankruptcy unless it urgently secures short-term financing. The airline is also discussing a possible takeover with investors but said it could not guarantee a viable solution. Its shares fell 85% on Wednesday. Jet-fuel costs that rose sharply during the war involving Iran have intensified the cash crunch. Norse does not hedge fuel purchases and reported a $94.6 million loss in the first half of 2026. The suspension also disrupted Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) flights operated with Norse aircraft and crews. PIA said it would use its own fleet for UK services.
business.image_alt: Norse Atlantic suspends flights, warns of bankruptcy without urgent financing

business.title: FCC requires SpaceX to file disposal plans for higher-orbit AI satellites
business.summary: Newly detailed terms of the U.S. Federal Communications Commission’s license for SpaceX’s proposed Starmind network require additional disposal plans for satellites flying above 600 kilometers and permit radio links as a backup to laser communications. Starmind is a planned constellation of up to one million satellites
business.content: Newly detailed terms of the U.S. Federal Communications Commission’s license for SpaceX’s proposed Starmind network require additional disposal plans for satellites flying above 600 kilometers and permit radio links as a backup to laser communications. Starmind is a planned constellation of up to one million satellites that would process artificial-intelligence workloads in orbit and relay results to Earth. SpaceX has said it aims to launch its first satellite in 2027. Sir Martin Sweeting, founder and executive chairman of Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd, said the laser links needed to move data between Earth and the satellites were not yet sufficiently developed to handle the expected volumes. The FCC is also reviewing applications from other companies for orbital data-center projects and has said it expects to decide on them quickly.
business.image_alt: FCC requires SpaceX to file disposal plans for higher-orbit AI satellites

business.title: Bank of England plans bank capital cuts, flags AI debt risks
business.summary: The Bank of England (BoE) said on Thursday it plans to reduce capital requirements tied to UK domestic lending risks by 0.27 percentage points of risk-weighted assets for major lenders. Together with other recent changes, the measures would lower overall requirements by about 0.5 percentage points and free roughly £175
business.content: The Bank of England (BoE) said on Thursday it plans to reduce capital requirements tied to UK domestic lending risks by 0.27 percentage points of risk-weighted assets for major lenders. Together with other recent changes, the measures would lower overall requirements by about 0.5 percentage points and free roughly £175 billion in lending capacity. The central bank plans to consult on the proposals in the first half of 2027. The BoE also warned that rapid borrowing in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector and increasingly complex, circular financing could spread losses across markets. Hyperscalers are expected to issue more than $305 billion in bonds this year. The central bank also urged financial firms to prepare for AI and quantum advances that could compromise encryption.
business.image_alt: Bank of England plans bank capital cuts, flags AI debt risks

business.title: Eurozone leaders back De Cos as ECB faces French debt strains
business.summary: Eurozone leaders backed former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos to lead the European Central Bank from Feb. 7, 2027, as French borrowing costs and inflation rise. Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, twice the ECB’s 2% target, and policymakers have raised interest rates twice this year. Investors have
business.content: Eurozone leaders backed former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos to lead the European Central Bank from Feb. 7, 2027, as French borrowing costs and inflation rise. Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, twice the ECB’s 2% target, and policymakers have raised interest rates twice this year. Investors have driven up French borrowing costs over concerns about public debt, the budget deficit and political uncertainty. The ECB can buy government bonds only if it judges market moves unwarranted or disorderly. Analysts expect de Cos to give weight to growth and financial stability, but say the leadership change alone is unlikely to alter near-term rate policy. The European Council has also put forward Germany’s Markus Brunnermeier as chief economist and France’s Laurence Boone for the executive board’s market-operations role. The European Parliament is due to hold a hearing on Dec. 7, with EU leaders expected to finalize the appointments at their Dec. 17 meeting.
business.image_alt: Eurozone leaders back De Cos as ECB faces French debt strains

business.title: Musk pledges annual SpaceX share gifts as stock rises overnight
business.summary: Elon Musk says he will donate another SpaceX share to every child in the United States each year, adding an annual pledge to SpaceX’s plan to donate one share to each active Trump Account under the program Congress established in 2025. Musk said he would personally match SpaceX’s contribution but has not specified whet
business.content: Elon Musk says he will donate another SpaceX share to every child in the United States each year, adding an annual pledge to SpaceX’s plan to donate one share to each active Trump Account under the program Congress established in 2025. Musk said he would personally match SpaceX’s contribution but has not specified whether he will distribute his personal shares or future annual gifts through Trump Accounts. SpaceX shares rose 7.47% in overnight trading on Blue Ocean ATS after Musk’s post, while regular U.S. exchanges were closed for Thanksgiving. The stock had finished Wednesday up 1.30%. The total value of the two-share gift depends on the share price and how many children ultimately receive it. The number of active Trump Accounts remains unclear. SpaceX plans to transfer its contribution in December, while Musk said his personal share would follow when his lockup expires in June 2027. The company and Musk have not explained how or when they will distribute the newly announced annual gifts.
business.image_alt: Musk pledges annual SpaceX share gifts as stock rises overnight

science.title: Engineered chromosome
science.summary: Researchers have engineered TALhesin, a molecular tether that reduced premature chromosome separation in older mouse eggs, and adapted it to bind human chromosomes in donated eggs. In 17-month-old mice, the share of eggs without premature separation errors rose from 46.7% to 74.1% after treatment. Age-related loss of c
science.content: Researchers have engineered TALhesin, a molecular tether that reduced premature chromosome separation in older mouse eggs, and adapted it to bind human chromosomes in donated eggs. In 17-month-old mice, the share of eggs without premature separation errors rose from 46.7% to 74.1% after treatment. Age-related loss of cohesin, the protein complex that normally holds chromosome halves together, can lead to eggs with abnormal chromosome counts and contribute to failed fertility treatment and pregnancy loss. The human experiments demonstrated chromosome binding, not a reduction in errors or improved fertility. The researchers say further efficacy and safety studies are needed before clinical use; fertility specialist Dunja Baston-Büst said the approach is not readily compatible with standard in vitro fertilization (IVF) procedures.

science.title: Quantum studies show progress and limits in computing advantage
science.summary: Researchers demonstrated magic-state cultivation on a superconducting processor, using a protocol predicted to reduce the cost of a resource needed for fault-tolerant universal quantum computing. Separately, a team led by Google Quantum AI and Stanford reported a classical algorithm whose runtime nearly matches that of
science.content: Researchers demonstrated magic-state cultivation on a superconducting processor, using a protocol predicted to reduce the cost of a resource needed for fault-tolerant universal quantum computing. Separately, a team led by Google Quantum AI and Stanford reported a classical algorithm whose runtime nearly matches that of quantum simulation for certain sparse random Hamiltonians. A third study, which analyzed quantum linear solvers for neural-network training, found that realistic end-to-end speedups emerge only under highly restrictive conditions. Gradient preparation scales with the number of model parameters and can erase gains from the quantum solver itself. The study estimated that crossover scenarios would require models exceeding 10^20 parameters and computation times above 10^19 seconds.
science.image_alt: Quantum studies show progress and limits in computing advantage

science.title: Hera team weighs CubeSat route changes after finding asteroid debris
science.summary: Scientists on the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Hera mission are assessing whether to change the approach routes for two small probes, known as CubeSats, after finding hundreds of boulders around the Didymos asteroid system. The rocks could strike and damage the probes. Hera is examining Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA’s
science.content: Scientists on the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Hera mission are assessing whether to change the approach routes for two small probes, known as CubeSats, after finding hundreds of boulders around the Didymos asteroid system. The rocks could strike and damage the probes. Hera is examining Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA’s DART spacecraft struck in 2022 to test deflection. Images released Nov. 25 show a stadium-sized crater and chaotic tumbling. Planetary scientist Naomi Murdoch said the boulders range from the size of a football to that of a washing machine. Researchers have not determined whether DART’s impact created them. Hera is due to move within 13 kilometers of the asteroids in December, with the CubeSats scheduled for deployment in January 2027. Mission teams are evaluating whether the debris requires revised routes.
science.image_alt: Hera team weighs CubeSat route changes after finding asteroid debris

science.title: Researchers identify possible largest known scorpion, over one meter long
science.summary: Researchers have identified Praearcturus gigas, a scorpion known from a fossil found in the United Kingdom dating to about 415 million years ago, as a candidate for the largest known scorpion. They estimated that the animal exceeded one meter in length. A new analysis combining CT scans with traditional fossil tracings
science.content: Researchers have identified Praearcturus gigas, a scorpion known from a fossil found in the United Kingdom dating to about 415 million years ago, as a candidate for the largest known scorpion. They estimated that the animal exceeded one meter in length. A new analysis combining CT scans with traditional fossil tracings resolved decades of uncertainty over its classification. Paleontologist Richie Howard and colleagues infer that it hunted both on land and in water; terrestrial ecosystems were still developing at the time. The researchers suggest that the absence of other large predators may have enabled its large size, while later competition may have contributed to its decline.
science.image_alt: Researchers identify possible largest known scorpion, over one meter long

science.title: Global temperatures exceed pre-industrial average by 2°C for a week as El Niño intensifies
science.summary: Preliminary data from Copernicus, the European Union’s climate-monitoring service, show global temperatures stayed more than 2°C above the 1850–1900 average for seven consecutive days, reaching 2.25°C above that baseline on Monday. These daily readings do not establish that the Paris Agreement’s temperature limit has b
science.content: Preliminary data from Copernicus, the European Union’s climate-monitoring service, show global temperatures stayed more than 2°C above the 1850–1900 average for seven consecutive days, reaching 2.25°C above that baseline on Monday. These daily readings do not establish that the Paris Agreement’s temperature limit has been breached: that target is assessed over at least 20 years. Scientists attribute the spike to long-term human-caused warming combined with a strong El Niño. The record run coincided with COP31 climate negotiations in Turkey, where nearly 200 countries failed to agree on language about moving away from fossil fuels. The UK Met Office forecasts an unusually sharp rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide in 2027 as drought weakens natural carbon sinks; one estimate puts the year-to-year increase at about 3.5 parts per million. The current El Niño began in June and is expected to continue until at least March.
science.image_alt: Global temperatures exceed pre-industrial average by 2°C for a week as El Niño intensifies

science.title: Meteor fireball streaks across Great Lakes during Indiana drone show
science.summary: A bright meteor flashed across the sky over the Great Lakes region Wednesday. The light was visible over eastern Michigan around 7:40 p.m., with sightings reported in neighboring states. In Fort Wayne, Indiana, it crossed the sky during the city’s Thanksgiving Eve Night of Lights drone display, where spectators capture
science.content: A bright meteor flashed across the sky over the Great Lakes region Wednesday. The light was visible over eastern Michigan around 7:40 p.m., with sightings reported in neighboring states. In Fort Wayne, Indiana, it crossed the sky during the city’s Thanksgiving Eve Night of Lights drone display, where spectators captured it on video. Michigan meteorologist Blake Hansen identified the light as a meteor, and a NASA satellite detected it as though it were a burst of lightning, according to WZZM. A separate local report described a bright green fireball over Northeast Ohio, while Cleveland television station WKYC also published footage of what it identified as a fireball meteor.
science.image_alt: Meteor fireball streaks across Great Lakes during Indiana drone show

science.title: OpenAI says model established theoretical speed limit for matrix multiplication
science.summary: OpenAI said on Nov. 25 that an internal artificial intelligence model had established a theoretical speed limit for multiplying matrices, a question that had occupied mathematicians and computer scientists for more than half a century. The previous week, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a Claude-assisted
science.content: OpenAI said on Nov. 25 that an internal artificial intelligence model had established a theoretical speed limit for multiplying matrices, a question that had occupied mathematicians and computer scientists for more than half a century. The previous week, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The Riemann proof is encoded in more than 17 million lines of Lean, a proof-checking language. Human review continues, and a mathematician interviewed by NPR said the code passed checks despite its scale. Some mathematicians warn that mass-producing results could strain research and education; others say AI lets them explore unfamiliar mathematical techniques more quickly.
science.image_alt: OpenAI says model established theoretical speed limit for matrix multiplication

science.title: Astronomers warn SpaceX’s million-satellite plan could obscure telescope images
science.summary: A peer-reviewed simulation suggests SpaceX’s proposed Starmind network could leave hundreds or thousands of satellites visible to the naked eye at once and obscure up to 28% of images from Chile’s Very Large Telescope, even if the satellites are substantially dimmed. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission authorize
science.content: A peer-reviewed simulation suggests SpaceX’s proposed Starmind network could leave hundreds or thousands of satellites visible to the naked eye at once and obscure up to 28% of images from Chile’s Very Large Telescope, even if the satellites are substantially dimmed. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission authorized SpaceX on Nov. 25 to deploy as many as one million satellites for orbital artificial-intelligence computing, potentially increasing the number of operational satellites to about 50 times the current total. The study’s author, European Southern Observatory astronomer Olivier Hainaut, modeled the effects of existing and proposed satellite constellations. The telescope-image estimate applies to observations taken two hours after nightfall. The European Southern Observatory has called for international oversight, while the FCC said SpaceX’s commitment to coordinate with the National Science Foundation was sufficient for optical astronomy. The authorization focuses on radio-frequency use and the FCC’s orbital-debris rules, rather than a separate review of optical astronomy or launch emissions. SpaceX must place its first satellite in orbit by November 2033, with deployment milestones running through 2040.
science.image_alt: Astronomers warn SpaceX’s million-satellite plan could obscure telescope images

sports.title: Eagles erase 21-point deficit, beat Cowboys on Elliott
sports.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III led a comeback from 21 points down against the Dallas Cowboys, setting up kicker Jake Elliott’s 59-yard field goal with two seconds left for a 39-38 Thanksgiving victory in Arlington, Texas. The comeback was the largest in an NFL Thanksgiving game and gave the Eagles conse
sports.content: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III led a comeback from 21 points down against the Dallas Cowboys, setting up kicker Jake Elliott’s 59-yard field goal with two seconds left for a 39-38 Thanksgiving victory in Arlington, Texas. The comeback was the largest in an NFL Thanksgiving game and gave the Eagles consecutive wins after a seven-game losing streak. Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another, while Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two scores. Dallas led 31-10 late in the third quarter and still held a 14-point lead in the fourth. The Cowboys fell to 5-7, while Philadelphia improved to 4-7. The Eagles visit Arizona on Dec. 6, and the Cowboys play at Seattle on Dec. 7.
sports.image_alt: Eagles erase 21-point deficit, beat Cowboys on Elliott

sports.title: Bills beat Chiefs 13-10 on Bass
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on Nov. 26 in Orchard Park, New York, on Tyler Bass’s 57-yard field goal as time expired. Linebacker Joe Andreessen partially blocked Kansas City punter Matt Araiza’s final punt, and Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Chiefs’ 39-yard line, setting up Bass’s attem
sports.content: The Buffalo Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on Nov. 26 in Orchard Park, New York, on Tyler Bass’s 57-yard field goal as time expired. Linebacker Joe Andreessen partially blocked Kansas City punter Matt Araiza’s final punt, and Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Chiefs’ 39-yard line, setting up Bass’s attempt with four seconds left. The victory extended Buffalo’s winning streak to seven and improved its record to an AFC-best 10-1. Rain, wind and cold limited both offenses. Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen completed 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards and threw two red-zone interceptions, while running back James Cook carried 32 times for 117 yards and scored the Bills’ only touchdown. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw for 174 yards without a touchdown; Emmett Johnson scored Kansas City’s lone touchdown on a one-yard run. The win gives Buffalo the head-to-head tiebreaker over Kansas City in the AFC seeding race. The Chiefs fell to 8-3 and, before Denver’s Friday game, trailed the Broncos by half a game in the AFC West. Buffalo next faces New England in Week 13, while Kansas City visits the Los Angeles Rams on Dec. 3.

sports.content: Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has called for focus and collective responsibility before his first home match, after a 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting left him without a win in his first two games. The draw followed a 4-0 loss to Liverpool. United remain 19th in the Premier League, with one win from their first 11 league matches. Pochettino said he was proud of the players’ character and felt their performance reflected the style he wants, while acknowledging that the team must improve its concentration and defensive habits. He defended goalkeeper Senne Lammens after the late mistake that cost United victory, saying the team must support him and take collective responsibility. Striker Joshua Zirkzee also urged United to assess their own performance rather than blame refereeing decisions, though he said those calls had an impact. Pochettino will next seek his first win against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday, November 28.

sports.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack exposed personal and business information before election
sports.summary: FIFA, world football’s governing body, confirmed that a criminal cyberattack allowed unauthorized access to a limited amount of personal and business information. The organization has not disclosed when the intrusion occurred, whose data was accessed or precisely which records were involved. It said it is working with
sports.content: FIFA, world football’s governing body, confirmed that a criminal cyberattack allowed unauthorized access to a limited amount of personal and business information. The organization has not disclosed when the intrusion occurred, whose data was accessed or precisely which records were involved. It said it is working with law enforcement. A group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot of alleged FIFA files on November 19 and appeared to claim responsibility three days later, after a post alleged that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had leaked. Reports citing people familiar with the breach say intruders compromised less than 0.1% of FIFA’s data by impersonating staff rather than exploiting a system failure. FIFA President Gianni Infantino is seeking another term after abandoning a plan to sell investors a stake in World Cup commercial rights. Reports say files tied to that proposal were not accessed. Infantino faces Japan’s Kozo Tashima and French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo in the election scheduled for March 18.

sports.content: Sunderland let an early second-half lead slip in a 1-1 home draw with Jagiellonia Białystok in the Europa League on November 26. Sunderland’s Timur Tutierov headed in Enzo Le Fée’s cross in the 47th minute, but Jagiellonia’s Kamil Józwiak equalised five minutes later after intercepting Reinildo Mandava’s attempted back-pass. The point left Sunderland 13th with eight points from five matches, inside the knockout play-off places. They still have away games against AC Milan and Anderlecht and a home match against Levski Sofia in January. Head coach Régis Le Bris made six changes after the goalless draw with Aston Villa, saying he needed to manage the squad ahead of upcoming fixtures. He also said recurring errors had again cost Sunderland.

sports.content: Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract extension, keeping him at Elland Road until summer 2029 and ending speculation over a possible move to Manchester United. The 29-year-old joined Leeds as a free agent from Everton in 2025 and has become a key part of their attack. Calvert-Lewin has five goals and one assist in 11 Premier League appearances this season, including a penalty and an assist in Leeds’ 4-1 win at Chelsea. Leeds are seventh, four points from the Champions League places, and face Coventry on Saturday. The new deal removes a release clause that could have allowed a January move below his market value, GiveMeSport reports. Leeds have extended several players’ contracts, while midfielder Ao Tanaka is also understood to have agreed terms on a new deal.

sports.content: The Chicago Bears rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 on Thanksgiving, taking sole possession of the NFC North lead. Quarterback Caleb Williams found wide receiver Rome Odunze for a six-yard touchdown with three seconds left, giving Chicago its first lead of the game. The Bears improved to 9-2; Detroit fell to 8-3. The Lions had led for 53 minutes and 31 seconds. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three touchdowns, including a 70-yard score that put Detroit ahead 35-24. Williams finished with 345 passing yards and two touchdowns, both to Odunze. A rookie safety’s interception and a fourth-down tackle of Gibbs helped Chicago regain possession for its final drive. The teams’ division records could matter in a playoff tiebreaker, and they are scheduled to meet again in Week 17. The Bears’ next game is against Jacksonville on Dec. 6. Tight end Colston Loveland left with a knee injury, and Bears coach Ben Johnson had no postgame update on his status.

sports.content: Great Britain beat Germany 2-1 in Bologna on Thursday, 26 November, to reach the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019. Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the quarter-final with a 6-2, 7-6(8-6) doubles win over Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz, after Cameron Norrie beat Jan-Lennard Struff and world No. 1 Alexander Zverev defeated Arthur Fery in singles. Britain faces Spain on Saturday, 28 November, for a place in the final. Norrie, ranked 52nd, saved four break points at 2-2 in the deciding set against 39th-ranked Struff, then won 12 of the next 14 points to take the match 6-3, 3-6, 6-2. Zverev levelled the tie with a 6-3, 6-2 win over Fery in 70 minutes, leaving the doubles to decide the quarter-final. The victory extends Britain captain Leon Smith’s final Davis Cup campaign. He has led Britain since 2010 and will leave the role after the tournament. Britain is seeking its first title since 2015, while Spain advanced without using Carlos Alcaraz, who had been set to play doubles if needed. Spain captain David Ferrer said Alcaraz could play against Britain but had not yet decided whether to select him.
